excerpt: Engineers have created a new solar panel design inspired by honeycomb structures found in beehives. This innovation addresses the issue of sunlight reflecting off flat panels at oblique angles. It could also adapt to applications beyond rooftops, such as vehicles and aerospace equipment.

Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Madrid, Sarah Morris.

headline: Israel kills senior member of Hamas's military wing in Gaza strike

headline: 'Record number of women elected' to US Congress & governorships across country in midterm elections
excerpt: Following the 2026 US midterm elections, Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Politico Senior National Politics Reporter Lauren Fedor. She discusses the growing number of Democratic women elected to Congress and governorships, particularly mothers of young children. “There was a realisation across the map that perhaps moms were the best messenger for this,” she explains, pointing to voters' concerns about “the cost of living, affordability, how to make ends meet.”

headline: Iran claims drone attack on US military base in Bahrain
excerpt: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September as blasts rocked the capital, Manama. It comes after Iran targeted an airbase in the US-allied island state, ending a long lull in strikes during the Middle East War and comes as negotiations to end the conflict remain at a stalemate, with the US maintaining its naval blockade and Iran its stranglehold over the strait of Hormuz. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

headline: Canaries urge government action after 2,200 migrants reach the islands in 48h
excerpt: Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants have arrived by boat to the Canary Islands this weekend. The Spanish islands are one of the main entry points into Europe for migrants from Africa. The Spanish Interior Ministry says more than 13,000 arrived there between January and the end of last month. Details and analysis by Andrew Hilliar, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.

headline: Jensen Huang: The French Connection
excerpt: President Trump is heading to Asia in a few days time, and will meet President Putin and President Xi. There's likely to be one fewer tech giants at the table, Jensen Huang, newly resigned from Nvidia, over the suspected spy affair.

headline: Santa school in full swing in London ahead of Christmas celebrations
excerpt: It may still be November but it's beginning to look a lot like Christmas in South London, as many Santa impersonators are heading to school for their festive training. The school, organised by an event company called Ministry of Fun, brings together Santas, elves, and Mrs Clauses to share experiences, practice belly laughs and learn how to bring the magic of Christmas to life. Story by Rachael Griffiths.

headline: A deep dive into Ivory Coast's solar energy goals
excerpt: Can Ivory Coast, which remains heavily dependent on fossil fuels, turn to solar power to make its energy consumption greener and more sustainable? We visited the country's new solar power plant in Ferkessédougou, in the north of the country. Inaugurated in July, it is expected to generate nearly 90 gigawatt-hours of electricity a year. Report by Julia Guggenheim.

headline: Why the Nvidia scandal is bad news for Europe’s AI ambitions
excerpt: Nvidia's Jensen Huang poured money into open-source AI, from French-founded Hugging Face to chips for Mistral's data centres, and fought Washington's attempts to restrict it. With Huang gone and China hawks emboldened, Tech 24 asks whether Europe's AI ambitions have lost their most powerful ally, and whether he was ever the champion Europe needed.

headline: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
excerpt: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting.

headline: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
excerpt: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris.

headline: The week in pictures: Spain protests, Pope Leo's Peru 'homecoming' and Rocky fans in Philly
excerpt: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images, from angry protests over a housing crisis that has dominated Spain's election campaign, to Leo XIV's visit to his adopted homeland Peru and "Rocky" fans marking 50 years since the release of boxing movie classic.

headline: French Ciryl Gane retains MMA heavyweaight title agianst Josh Hokit

headline: Bahrain says air defences destroyed several Iranian drones attacking US base
excerpt: Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday, its first such warnings since September. Diplomatic efforts to end the almost nine-month conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, with sporadic attacks continuing. Separate overnight strikes on Taganrog city killed an electricity substation engineer, according to the regional governor.

excerpt: Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in the Philippine capital Manila on Sunday. headline: Air travel issues persist in the US after nationwide ground stop

The International Organisation of the Francophonie is set to elect its next secretary-general on Monday for a four-year term, but escalating friction between Rwanda, which has led the OIF for eight years, and the Democratic Republic of Congo has thrown the summit into crisis. headline: Illegal mining threatens French Guiana forests and indigenous communities
excerpt: In French Guiana, the fight against illegal gold mining is rapidly being lost and creating an environmental and health disaster, according to the World Wildlife Fund. During an aerial survey in early August, park rangers counted 239 illegal sites within the protected area in record.

excerpt: This week's Microsoft outage highlighted the risks of relying on a single technology provider for essential services. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours, impacting millions of users across more than 70 countries – from government agencies to airlines to hospitals and small businesses. Are we too reliant on technology? Analysis by Marcel Saucet, research associate at the University of San Diego School of Law.

Emphasizing the need for individuals to set aside ego and self-interest, he illustrated his points with lessons from the Mahabharata, stressing that unity is key to overcoming challenges.

She dominated the women's 48kg category with a decisive 5-0 victory over Algeria's Bouthaina Bensalah. This monumental achievement, alongside L Ambekar Meetei's win, signals India's first double gold in boxing at this event.

This effort focuses on protecting habitats for the rare Bi-State sage-grouse while allowing continued agricultural activities. A permanent conservation agreement prevents non-agricultural development and preserves the land's ecological value. Additionally, a future grant will facilitate restoration work across 350 acres to control invasive grass and support biodiversity.

excerpt: The historic Union Street School in Leesburg, Virginia has reopened as a museum and community centre. After a refurbishment costing around $6.2 million, the building now serves to educate about Black history. Initially established in 1884, it provided education to Black children during segregation until 1958. The new museum aims to preserve memories and share the stories of those associated with the school.

With a top cruising speed of 300 kilometers per hour and a range of up to 400 kilometers, the CE-25A employs advanced distributed electric propulsion technology, signaling a new era for electric flight.

After suffering serious injuries, he was taken to Terna Hospital but tragically died three days later. The police swiftly apprehended the three attackers, charging them with murder and recovering the stolen belongings shortly thereafter.

He called for the ousting of the BJP government, highlighting the need for social justice. Akhilesh criticized the ruling party's record on Dalit issues, which includes the vandalism of Dr. BR Ambedkar's statues. In a joint statement after a summit in Brussels, the UK and EU confirmed agreements that will scrap checks on the trade in plant and animal products, link their emissions trading schemes and let 100,000 young adults from each side live and work in the other's countries for up to three years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

headline: Russia pummels Ukraine with massive strikes, missile hits Poland

Hours earlier, Russia's Vladimir Putin vowed a "painful" response to Kyiv's strikes on Moscow's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with China's Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.

headline: 'GTA VI': When the biggest-ever entertainment release becomes the biggest headline

Our guest is Margaret Wallace, a video game developer and an associate professor of the practice of media innovation at Boston University.

headline: Does staggered consent actually protect young people?
